cards.front: What should you remember from Measurement of Time and Motion?
cards.back: Measurement of 8 Time and Motion Prerna and her younger sister are watching a sports channel on television.

cards.front: What should you remember from Measurement of Time and Motion?
cards.back: Prerna enjoys running and she has been declared the fastest runner among the girls in her district for winning the 100 metre sprint at an interschool competition held at the district level.

cards.front: What should you remember from Measurement of Time and Motion?
cards.back: She dreams of representing India at the international level in 100 metre sprint contests in future.

cards.front: What should you remember from Measurement of Time and Motion?
cards.back: While watching the rerun of sprints at the Olympic games held in the past, Prerna is always amazed that the measurement of the time taken for the race is so advanced that they could identify the winner even when two sprinters seemed to cross the ﬁnish line almost together.

cards.front: What should you remember from Measurement of Time and Motion?
cards.back: However, in her school, the sports teacher only used a special kind of watch called a ‘stopwatch’ for timing the school races.

cards.front: What should you remember from Measurement of Time and Motion?
cards.back: She had noticed her mother wearing a watch on her wrist and her sister looking at her mobile phone when she needed to check the time.

cards.front: What should you remember from Measurement of Time and Motion?
cards.back: Her uncle used a Braille watch and had recently acquired a talking watch that announced the time at the touch of a button.

cards.front: What should you remember from Measurement of Time and Motion?
cards.back: There was also a large clock on the wall near the school entrance.
